title: What If One Icelandic Volcano Shut Down Europe's Skies?

scenes.text: What if one Icelandic volcano shut down the skies over Europe? In 2010, one did.
Eyjafjallajökull erupted on April 14, 2010. By April 16, 16,000 of Europe's 28,000 daily flights were cancelled.
Before then, the rule was simple: any ash above zero meant the airspace was unsafe.
In 1982, a British Airways jet flew through volcanic ash and lost all four engines. The crew restarted three and landed safely.
Over about eight days, roughly 107,000 flights were cancelled and around 10 million passengers were affected.
Airlines lost about 1.7 billion dollars. Regulators then set an ash limit of 2 milligrams per cubic meter, later raised to 4.

description:
What if one Icelandic volcano shut down Europe's skies?
In April 2010, Eyjafjallajökull's ash cancelled around 107,000 flights and affected about 10 million passengers, the biggest shutdown of European air traffic since World War Two.
